gloss: rise, arise, stand; stand firm, endure; raise up, set up, establish; standing-place, place; height
summary: The verb is to rise from lying or sitting and so to stand: to get up and act, to come on the scene, to rise against an enemy, to rise from the dead (Gen 19:1; Exo 1:8; Deu 19:11; Isa 26:19). What stands endures: a word, counsel, vow or kingdom that “stands” holds good and comes to pass, and Yahweh “makes stand” his covenant, his oath and his word, and raises up a judge, a prophet like Moses, and David’s seed (Isa 40:8; Gen 17:7; Num 23:19; Deu 18:15; 2Sa 7:12). Its nouns are מָקוֹם, the place where one stands, קוֹמָה, the height a thing stands to, and קָמָה, the grain standing in the field. Arabic qāma, maqām, Ugaritic qm, Punic qm and mqm and Geʿez qoma share the same senses, and the Peshitta’s qām and qyāmtā carry the word into the New Testament’s resurrection.

words.gloss: rise, arise, stand; stand firm, come to pass; (hiphil) raise up, set up, establish, confirm
words.summary: About 630 uses, three in four in the qal (rise, stand) and most of the rest in the hiphil (make stand: raise up, set up, establish). The late books add a piel “confirm, ratify” and the poets a polel “raise up (ruins)” and a hithpolel “rise up against”.

stems.gloss: rise, get up; arise; rise against; stand, hold one’s ground; stand, endure, come to pass; rise from the dead

senses.definition: To rise from lying, sitting or kneeling: the opposite of lying down and of sitting.

evidence.note: Speak of the words “when you sit in your house … and when you lie down (שָׁכְבְּךָ) and when you rise (קוּמֶךָ)”.
Lot was sitting in the gate of Sodom; “he rose to meet them”.
“Before grey hair you shall rise, and honour the face of the old man.”
“He did not know when she lay down or when she rose.”
Eglon “rose from the seat”.
Solomon rose from before the altar, from kneeling on his knees.
“You know my sitting down and my rising.”
“They bow down and fall, but we rise and stand upright.”

senses.definition: To get up in order to do something, often before a second verb: “arise, go”, “he arose and went”.

evidence.note: Abraham rose early, saddled his donkey, “and arose and went to the place of which God had told him”.
“Arise, go to Nineveh”; Jonah “arose to flee to Tarshish” (Jon 1:3).
The second time, “Jonah arose and went to Nineveh”.
“Arise, cross this Jordan.”
“Arise! For this is the day that Yahweh has given Sisera into your hand.”
“Arise, shine, for your light has come.”
“Arise, go with them.”

senses.gloss: arise (of Yahweh, to act for his people)
senses.definition: Yahweh’s rising is his going into action: to scatter his enemies, to save the oppressed, to judge the earth.

evidence.note: When the ark set out Moses said, “Arise (קוּמָה), Yahweh, and let your enemies be scattered, and let those who hate you flee before you.”
The same words: “Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered.”
“Because of the oppression of the poor … now I will arise, says Yahweh; I will set him in the safety he longs for.”
“Arise, Yahweh, to your resting place, you and the ark of your strength”; repeated at the temple’s dedication (2Ch 6:41).
“Arise, O God, judge the earth, for you shall inherit all the nations.”
“Now I will arise, says Yahweh; now I will be exalted.”
“When he arises to terrify the earth.”
“Wait for me … for the day of my rising up to the prey.”

senses.gloss: rise against, rise up as an enemy
senses.definition: To rise up with hostile intent; the participle קָמִים is “those who rise against”, enemies.

evidence.note: “Your enemies who rise against you (הַקָּמִים עָלֶיךָ).”
“In the greatness of your majesty you overthrow those who rise against you (קָמֶיךָ).”
“Cain rose against Abel his brother and killed him.”
One who hates his neighbour, lies in wait, “rises against him” and strikes him.
“False witnesses have risen against me.”
“A daughter rises against her mother”; Jesus takes up the verse (Mat 10:35–36).
Peshitta: “children will rise (ܢܩܘܡܘܢ) against their parents.”
“You subdued under me those who rose against me (קָמַי).”
“My leanness rises up against me.”

senses.definition: Of a person or a generation: to come into being or into power.

evidence.note: “A new king arose over Egypt who did not know Joseph”; quoted by Stephen with the same word in the Peshitta (Act 7:18).
Peshitta ܩܡ, Greek ἀνέστη.
“There has not arisen a prophet since in Israel like Moses.”
“Another generation arose after them who did not know Yahweh.”
“Until I, Deborah, arose, arose a mother in Israel.”
“If a prophet or a dreamer of dreams arises among you.”
“After you shall none arise like you.”
Peshitta: “many false prophets will arise (ܢܩܘܡܘܢ)”.

senses.definition: To stand and not give way before an enemy, a judge or God.

evidence.note: “The sons of Israel could not stand before their enemies; they turned their backs.”
“Before his indignation who can stand (יַעֲמוֹד)? And who can rise up (יָקוּם) in the heat of his anger?”
“The wicked shall not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous.”
“Who shall stand in his holy place?”
“How shall Jacob stand? For he is small.”
“A righteous man falls seven times and rises up.”
“When I fall, I shall arise.”

senses.gloss: stand, hold good, come to pass
senses.definition: Of a word, counsel, plan, vow or kingdom: to stand and so to endure and be carried out; the opposite of a word that falls or comes to nothing.

evidence.note: “The grass withers, the flower fades, but the word of our God shall stand forever”; quoted at 1Pe 1:24–25.
“Many are the plans in a man’s heart, but the counsel of Yahweh, it shall stand.”
Of the kings’ plot against Judah: “It shall not stand, and it shall not come to pass.”
“As I have purposed, so it shall stand.”
“My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure.”
“They shall know whose word will stand, mine or theirs.”
“Speak a word, and it shall not stand, for God is with us.”
“Now your kingdom shall not stand.”
If her father keeps silent, “all her vows shall stand, and every bond … shall stand”.
The vow of a widow or a divorced woman “shall stand against her”.
“One witness shall not rise up against a man … at the mouth of two witnesses or at the mouth of three witnesses shall a matter stand”; quoted at Mat 18:16 and 2Co 13:1.
Peshitta ܬܩܘܡ, Greek σταθῇ.

senses.gloss: be made sure (to someone), pass to (of property)
senses.definition: Of land bought or redeemed: to stand to the buyer as his.

evidence.note: “The field of Ephron … and the cave and every tree in it stood (וַיָּקָם) to Abraham as a possession.”
If he redeems the field he consecrated, adding a fifth, “it shall stand to him”.
A house in a walled city not redeemed within the year “shall stand” to the buyer for ever.

senses.definition: Of the dead lying in the dust: to rise to life again, set beside “live” and “awake”.

evidence.note: “Your dead shall live; my corpses shall rise (יְקוּמוּן). Awake and sing, dwellers in the dust.”
“Man lies down and does not rise; till the heavens are no more they shall not awake, nor be roused from their sleep.”
Of the oppressors: “They are dead, they shall not live; Raphaites, they shall not rise.”
“Will you do wonders for the dead? Shall the Raphaites rise and praise you?”
The dead man thrown into Elisha’s grave touched his bones, “and lived, and rose on his feet”.
“Fallen, she shall rise no more, the virgin of Israel.”
“I know that my redeemer lives, and at the last he shall stand (יָקוּם) upon the dust.”

senses.definition: Of an old man’s eyes: to stand still, set, so that he cannot see.

evidence.note: Eli was ninety-eight, “and his eyes were set (קָמָה), and he could not see”.
“Ahijah could not see, for his eyes were set (קָמוּ) because of his age.”

stems.gloss: raise, set up, erect; help up; raise up (a person); raise up seed; establish, confirm, carry out

senses.definition: To make a thing stand: the tabernacle, a pillar, stones, an altar, an image.

evidence.note: “Moses set up (וַיָּקֶם) the tabernacle, and laid its sockets, and set its boards … and set up (וַיָּקֶם) its pillars.”
“You shall set up the tabernacle according to its plan which you were shown on the mountain.”
“On the day the tabernacle was set up, the cloud covered it.”
The Kohathites set out carrying the holy things, “and they set up the tabernacle before they came”.
Joshua set up twelve stones in the midst of the Jordan.
“Nor shall you set up for yourselves a pillar.”
“You shall set up for yourself great stones and plaster them.”
“Go up, set up an altar to Yahweh on the threshing floor of Araunah.”
He set up the pillars Jachin and Boaz.
Manasseh set up altars for Baal.

senses.definition: To raise one who has fallen, literally and of the poor and the stumbling.

evidence.note: “You shall not see your brother’s donkey or his ox fallen in the way … you shall surely help him lift it up.”
“If they fall, the one will lift up his companion; but woe to him who is alone when he falls, and has no second to lift him up.”
“He raises the poor from the dust, he lifts the needy from the ash heap”; again Psa 113:7.
“She is forsaken on her land; there is none to raise her up.”
“Your words have upheld him who was stumbling.”
“Raise me up, that I may repay them.”

senses.gloss: raise up (a judge, prophet, king, shepherd)
senses.definition: God’s causing a person to arise for a work: a deliverer, a prophet, a priest, a king of David’s line, or an adversary in judgment.

evidence.note: “A prophet from your midst, from your brothers, like me, Yahweh your God will raise up for you; to him you shall listen”; applied to Jesus at Act 3:22 and 7:37.
“I will raise up for them a prophet from among their brothers, like you, and I will put my words in his mouth.”
“Yahweh raised up judges, and they saved them from the hand of their plunderers.”
Yahweh raised up a saviour, Othniel; Ehud likewise (Jdg 3:15).
“I will raise up for myself a faithful priest.”
“I will raise up your seed after you, who shall come out of your body, and I will establish his kingdom.”
“I will raise up for David a righteous Branch, and he shall reign as king.”
“They shall serve Yahweh their God and David their king, whom I will raise up for them.”
“I will raise up over them one shepherd, my servant David.”
“I raised up some of your sons as prophets, and of your young men as Nazirites.”
“Yahweh raised up an adversary (שָׂטָן) to Solomon, Hadad the Edomite.”
“Behold, I am raising up the Chaldeans.”
“I will raise up evil against you out of your own house.”
Peter quotes Deu 18:15: Peshitta ܢܩܝܡ, Greek ἀναστήσει.

senses.gloss: raise up seed, a name (for the dead)
senses.definition: To give a dead brother an heir by his widow, so that his name stands in Israel.

evidence.note: “My husband’s brother refuses to raise up (לְהָקִים) for his brother a name in Israel.”
“Go in to your brother’s wife … and raise up seed for your brother.”
Qal: “The firstborn she bears shall rise (יָקוּם) on the name of his dead brother, that his name be not blotted out of Israel.”
“To raise up the name of the dead on his inheritance”; again Rut 4:10.
The Sadducees’ paraphrase of Deu 25:5–6: “his brother shall … raise up (Peshitta ܢܩܝܡ, Greek ἀναστήσει) seed for his brother.”

senses.gloss: establish, confirm, carry out (a covenant, oath, word, vow)
senses.definition: To make a covenant, oath or spoken word stand: to put it in force and carry it out; of a husband, to let a vow stand.

evidence.note: “I will establish my covenant between me and you and your seed after you … for an everlasting covenant.”
“I will establish my covenant with you; and you shall come into the ark.”
“I establish my covenant with you: never again shall all flesh be cut off by the waters of a flood.”
“I will establish the oath which I swore to Abraham your father.”
“God is not a man that he should lie … Has he spoken and will he not make it stand?”
“That he may establish the word which Yahweh swore to your fathers.”
“That he may establish his covenant which he swore to your fathers.”
“Yahweh has established his word that he spoke, and I have arisen (וָאָקֻם) in the place of David my father.”
After seventy years “I will establish my good word toward you, to bring you back to this place”.
“I will establish the good word that I spoke to the house of Israel.”
Of Saul: “He has not carried out my words.”
“Cursed is he who does not make stand the words of this law, to do them”; quoted at Gal 3:10.
Josiah’s covenant “to carry out the words of this covenant written in this book”.
“Every vow … her husband may make it stand (יְקִימֶנּוּ), or her husband may make it void (יְפֵרֶנּוּ).”
“Establish your word to your servant.”

senses.definition: To raise up what has fallen or died so that it lives and stands again: Israel, its tribes, David’s fallen tent.

evidence.note: “After two days he will revive us; on the third day he will raise us up (יְקִמֵנוּ), and we shall live before him.”
“In that day I will raise up the fallen tent of David … and raise up its ruins”; quoted by James at Act 15:16, where the Peshitta has ܐܩܝܡ.
“To raise up the tribes of Jacob and to restore the preserved of Israel.”

senses.definition: To make the storm stand still.

evidence.note: “He makes the storm stand (יָקֵם) to a calm, and its waves are still.”

stems.gloss: be set up; be raised; be carried out

senses.gloss: be set up, raised; be carried out
senses.definition: The passive of the hiphil: a structure set up, a man raised up, a command carried out.

evidence.note: “In the first month of the second year, on the first of the month, the tabernacle was set up (הוּקַם).”
“The oracle of the man who was raised on high (הֻקַם עָל), the anointed of the God of Jacob.”
“The words of Jonadab son of Rechab … have been carried out (הוּקַם): they have drunk no wine to this day.”

stems.gloss: confirm, ratify; establish (a custom); raise up

senses.definition: To make a transaction, an oath or an observance stand as binding; found in Ruth, Ezekiel, the Psalms and Esther.

evidence.note: “This was the custom in Israel concerning redeeming and exchanging, to confirm (לְקַיֵּם) any matter: a man drew off his sandal and gave it to his neighbour.”
Mordecai wrote “to establish among them” the keeping of the fourteenth and fifteenth of Adar year by year.
“The Jews established and took upon themselves and their seed … to keep these two days.”
“To establish these days of Purim in their times.”
“I have sworn, and I will confirm it, to keep your righteous judgments.”
False prophets say “Yahweh says”, though he has not sent them, “and they hope for the word to be confirmed”.
“My soul melts from grief; raise me up (קַיְּמֵנִי) according to your word.”

stems.gloss: raise up (ruins); rise up (as an enemy)

senses.definition: To raise again what lies in ruins.

evidence.note: Yahweh “establishes (מֵקִים) the word of his servant … who says of the cities of Judah, They shall be built, and I will raise up (אֲקוֹמֵם) its ruins”.
“You shall raise up the foundations of many generations.”
“They shall build the ancient ruins, they shall raise up the former desolations.”

senses.definition: Intransitive, of a people turning hostile.

evidence.note: “Of late my people has risen up as an enemy.”

senses.definition: To set oneself up against someone; the participle is “those who rise up against”, adversaries.

evidence.note: “Deliver me from my enemies, my God; set me on high from those who rise up against me (מִמִּתְקוֹמְמַי).”
“Let my enemy be as the wicked, and he who rises up against me as the unrighteous.”
“You who save by your right hand those who take refuge from those who rise up.”
“The heavens will reveal his iniquity, and the earth will rise up against him.”
“Do I not loathe those who rise up against you?” (written וּבִתְקוֹמְמֶיךָ).

evidence.locator: Deu.18.15, יָקִים → ἀναστήσει; Deu.18.18 אָקִים → ἀναστήσω; 2Sa.7.12 and Amo.9.11 the same; ἀνίστημι renders קוּם ×346

evidence.note: Peter quotes Deu 18:15: “A prophet will the Lord your God raise up (ἀναστήσει) for you from your brothers, like me”; again Act 7:37.
“God, having raised up (ἀναστήσας) his servant, sent him to you first.”
“Raise up (ἀναστήσει) seed for his brother.”
“Having raised up Jesus”, and in 13:34 “raised him from the dead”.
Exo 1:8: “another king arose (ἀνέστη)”.

evidence.locator: Deu.19.15, יָקוּם דָּבָר → σταθήσεται πᾶν ῥῆμα; ἵστημι renders קוּם ×73

evidence.note: “That at the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may stand (σταθῇ).”
“We establish (ἱστάνομεν) the law”; Peshitta ܡܩܝܡܝܢܢ.
Isa 40:8 quoted: “the word of the Lord abides (μένει) forever”; Peshitta ܩܝܡܐ.

parallels.note: “Awake”, “be roused”, beside rising from sleep and from death.
“Come to pass”, beside a plan’s standing.
“Establish”: raise up David’s seed and establish his kingdom.

opposites.note: Falling, against rising and being lifted up.
“Make void, annul”, against the hiphil “make stand” of a vow.

phrases.gloss: “Arise, Yahweh”: the call for Yahweh to go into action for his people
make a word stand: carry out a promise or command
raise up seed, a name, for a dead brother

words.gloss: standing-place; place, spot; one’s place; the place (of worship)
words.summary: The place where one stands, a noun of place from the verb: 401 uses. Any place or spot; a person’s own place, home or seat; the land Yahweh promised; and above all “the place which Yahweh will choose” for his name, where the feasts were to be kept. Arabic maqām “standing-place” and Punic mqm “place” are the same word.

senses.definition: A place, the ground where something is or stands.

evidence.note: “The place on which you are standing (עוֹמֵד) is holy ground”; quoted by Stephen (Act 7:33).
“Let the waters under the heavens be gathered to one place.”
Jacob came to a certain place, took one of the stones of the place, and lay down in that place.
“To the place where the rivers go, there they go again.”
“All go to one place: all are from the dust, and all return to the dust.”
“I will appoint you a place to which he may flee.”

senses.definition: The place that belongs to someone: his home or country, his station, his seat at table.

evidence.note: “Send me away, that I may go to my place and to my land.”
At the new moon meal the king sat on his seat, “and David’s place was empty”; again 1Sa 20:27.
Balak to Balaam: “Flee to your place.”
Of the dead: “He shall not return to his house, nor shall his place know him any more”; of man as grass, Psa 103:16.
Yahweh: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their guilt.”
“Yahweh is coming out of his place”; Isa 26:21.

senses.definition: The place Yahweh said he would give Israel, to which he led them.

evidence.note: Moses to Hobab: “We are setting out for the place of which Yahweh said, I will give it to you.”
“I send an angel before you … to bring you to the place that I have prepared.”
Yahweh went before them “to seek out a place for you to camp”.
“To bring you back to this place.”

senses.gloss: the place (of Yahweh’s name, of worship)
senses.definition: A place where Yahweh met men, and the one place he would choose to set his name, where sacrifices and the feasts were to be kept.

evidence.note: “To the place which Yahweh your God shall choose out of all your tribes to put his name there … there you shall come.”
The Passover is to be sacrificed “at the place which Yahweh your God shall choose to make his name dwell”.
On the third day Abraham saw “the place” afar off.
“How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of God.”
“It shall be eaten in a holy place.”
“Go to my place which was in Shiloh, where I made my name dwell at first, and see what I did to it”; and so to the house in Jerusalem (Jer 7:14).
“When they pray toward this place, hear in the place of your dwelling, in heaven.”
“Where is the house that you will build for me, and where is the place of my rest?”, quoted by Stephen (Act 7:49).

senses.definition: בִּמְקוֹם with a clause: in the place where, there where.

evidence.note: “In the place where it was said to them, You are not my people, it shall be said to them, Sons of the living God”; quoted at Rom 9:26.
“In the place where my lord the king shall be, whether for death or for life, there your servant will be.”

evidence.locator: Num.10.29, מָקוֹם → τόπον; Exo.3.5 → τόπος; Deu.12.5 → τόπον; τόπος renders מָקוֹם ×353

evidence.note: Exo 3:5: “the place (τόπος) on which you stand is holy ground.”
Hos 2:1: “in the place (τόπῳ) where it was said to them, You are not my people.”
Isa 66:1: “what is the place (τόπος) of my rest?”
“You say that in Jerusalem is the place (τόπος) where men ought to worship.”
“The Romans will come and take away both our place (τόπον) and our nation.”
“This Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place (τόπον).”
“I go to prepare a place (τόπον) for you.”

phrases.gloss: the place which Yahweh will choose
his place shall know him no more (of the dead and the perishing)

words.summary: How high a thing stands: the height of the ark, the tabernacle’s furniture and Solomon’s house, a man’s stature, and the lofty growth of a cedar, an image of pride (45 uses). Arabic qāmah and Geʿez qom are “stature, height” too.

senses.definition: The height of something built, given in cubits beside its length and breadth.

evidence.note: The ark: “three hundred cubits its length, fifty cubits its breadth, and thirty cubits its height (קוֹמָתָהּ).”
The ark of the covenant, “a cubit and a half its height”.
The house Solomon built, “thirty cubits its height”.
The man measured the wall: “the breadth one reed, and the height one reed.”

senses.definition: A person’s height as he stands, his full length.

evidence.note: “Do not look on his appearance or on the height of his stature … for Yahweh looks on the heart.”
“Saul fell at once his full length (מְלֹא קוֹמָתוֹ) to the ground.”
“This your stature is like a palm tree.”
Veils “on the head of every stature”, to hunt souls.

senses.definition: The tall growth of a cedar or vine, in the prophets an image of a proud king brought low.

evidence.note: “Assyria was a cedar in Lebanon … high of stature.”
“Because you were high in stature … and his heart was lifted up in his height.”
“The high of stature shall be hewn down, and the lofty shall be brought low.”
“I will cut down its tall cedars.”

evidence.locator: ὕψος renders קוֹמָה ×22 (Gen.6.15, Exo.25.10 and the measurements)

evidence.note: The city: “the length and the breadth and the height (ὕψος) of it are equal.”
Zacchaeus “was small of stature (ἡλικίᾳ)”; Peshitta ܩܘܡܬܐ.
“To the measure of the stature (ἡλικίας) of the fullness of Christ”; Peshitta ܩܘܡܬܐ.

words.summary: Grain standing in the field before it is cut (10 uses), from the qal “stand”. Its use rests on the verb: no cognate gives the noun itself.

senses.definition: Grain still standing in the field, ready for the sickle.

evidence.note: “From the time you first put the sickle to the standing grain you shall begin to count seven weeks”: the count to the Feast of Weeks of Lev 23:15–16.
“When you come into your neighbour’s standing grain, you may pluck ears with your hand, but you shall not put a sickle to your neighbour’s standing grain.”
If fire spreads and “stacked grain, or the standing grain, or the field” is consumed, he who kindled it shall pay.
Samson’s foxes burned “both the stacks and the standing grain”.
“As when the harvester gathers the standing grain.”
“They sow the wind and reap the whirlwind; standing grain with no head, it yields no meal.”
“Like grass on the housetops, blighted before it is grown up (לִפְנֵי קָמָה)”; again Isa 37:27.

words.gloss: what stands, living thing, all that exists
words.summary: “That which stands (up)”: every living thing on the ground (3 uses). A noun formed with a prefix from the verb, used only in the flood and of Korah’s company; its tie to the root rests on the verb’s “stand, exist” and the Jewish Aramaic use of קוּם “exist”.

senses.definition: Everything that stands and lives on the face of the ground, man and beast.

evidence.note: “He blotted out every יְקוּם that was on the face of the ground, from man to beast, to creeping thing, and to the birds of the heavens … and only Noah was left, and those with him in the ark.”
“Every יְקוּם that I have made I will blot out from the face of the ground.”
The earth swallowed Dathan and Abiram, their households, their tents, “and every יְקוּם that followed them”.
The New Testament’s one use is of the resurrection from the dead, not of the flood: the link is only the Greek’s “rising up”.

words.summary: One use, of those risen up against the righteous; the same sense as the qal participle קָמִים, and as Ugaritic qm “adversary”.

senses.definition: One who has risen up against another.

evidence.note: The righteous say, “Surely our adversaries (קִימָנוּ) are cut off, and fire has consumed what they left.”

words.summary: One use, the act of rising up, set against sitting down.

senses.definition: Getting up, the opposite of sitting down.

evidence.note: “Look at their sitting down and their rising up (קִימָתָם); I am their mocking song.”
“Set for the fall and rising again (ἀνάστασιν) of many in Israel”; Peshitta ܩܝܡܐ.
“He will rise again in the resurrection (ἀναστάσει) at the last day.”

words.summary: One use: Israel made to walk upright once the yoke of slavery was broken.

senses.definition: Standing tall, no longer bowed under a yoke.

evidence.note: “I broke the bars of your yoke and made you walk upright (קוֹמְמִיּוּת).”

words.summary: One use, in the curses of Leviticus: no ability to stand before enemies.

senses.definition: The ability to stand one’s ground.

evidence.note: “They shall stumble over one another as before the sword, when none pursues, and you shall have no power to stand (תְּקוּמָה) before your enemies.”

words.gloss: no rising against (him); or, a band, the people
words.summary: One use, at the end of a list of things stately in their going. Read as אַל + קוּם it is a king “against whom there is no rising up”; read as the Arabic article and qawm “people, company of men”, a king “with his band about him”. Either way it goes back to this root, but which reading is right is not clear.

senses.gloss: no rising up; or, his troop
senses.definition: A king with whom no one can contend, or a king with his people round him.

evidence.note: “The strutting rooster, the he-goat, and a king אַלְקוּם with him.”

words.gloss: arise, stand; endure; (aphel, haphel) set up, establish, appoint
words.summary: The Aramaic of Daniel and Ezra uses the verb as the Hebrew does: kings and kingdoms arise, God’s kingdom stands forever, and Nebuchadnezzar sets up his image, while God sets up kings and his own kingdom.

senses.definition: To get up; of kingdoms and kings, to arise in succession.

evidence.note: “After you shall arise another kingdom inferior to you.”
“These great beasts, which are four, are four kings who shall arise out of the earth.”
“Ten kings shall arise, and another shall arise after them.”
Nebuchadnezzar “rose in haste”.
The king arose at dawn and went in haste to the lions’ den.
Zerubbabel and Jeshua “arose and began to build the house of God”.
To the bear: “Arise, devour much flesh.”

senses.definition: To stand, of those attending the Ancient of Days and of an image; to stand fast and endure, of God’s kingdom.

evidence.note: God’s kingdom “shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand (תְּקוּם) forever”.
“Ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him.”
“I came near to one of those who stood by (קָאֲמַיָּא).”
The great image “stood before you”.

senses.definition: To make stand: an image, a kingdom, a ruler, a decree.

evidence.note: “In the days of those kings the God of heaven will set up (יְקִים) a kingdom which shall never be destroyed.”
Nebuchadnezzar made an image of gold and “set it up in the plain of Dura”.
The Most High “gives it to whom he will, and sets up over it the lowest of men”.
“Now, O king, establish the decree and sign the writing.”

senses.definition: To set up an image; to set up kings and officers in office; to establish a statute.

evidence.note: “He removes kings and sets up kings (וּמְהָקֵים מַלְכִין).”
The dedication of “the image which Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up”, repeated through the chapter.
“We will not serve your gods, nor worship the golden image which you have set up.”
“The Most High God rules in the kingdom of men, and sets up over it whom he will.”
Darius set over the kingdom a hundred and twenty satraps.
The king thought to set Daniel over the whole kingdom.
“No decree or statute which the king establishes may be changed.”
“They set the priests in their divisions and the Levites in their courses … as it is written in the book of Moses.”

stems.gloss: be made to stand, be raised up

senses.gloss: be made to stand, be raised
senses.definition: The passive: set on its feet, raised up.

evidence.note: The lion-beast “was lifted up from the earth and made to stand (הֳקִימַת) on two feet like a man”.
The bear “was raised up on one side”.

senses.definition: To put a statute in force.

evidence.note: “To establish (לְקַיָּמָה) a royal statute (קְיָם) and to make a firm decree.”

Jesus took the girl by the hand and said “ταλιθα κουμ (κοῦμι)”, which Mark translates “Little girl, I say to you, arise (ἔγειρε)”; and “immediately the girl arose (ἀνέστη) and walked” (Mrk 5:42). The Peshitta has ܛܠܝܬܐ ܩܘܡܝ.
“(Tr., txt., κοῦμ, Rec. κοῦμι) (Heb. imperat. masc., used as an interjection, קוּם), koum (arise): Mk 5:41.”

words.summary: Two uses, in the plot against Daniel: a statute the king makes stand.

senses.definition: A royal statute, something established so that it stands.

evidence.note: “To establish a royal statute (קְיָם) and to make a firm decree.”
“No decree or statute (קְיָם) which the king establishes may be changed.”

words.summary: Two uses: what stands and lasts, of Nebuchadnezzar’s kingdom kept for him and of the living God.

senses.definition: Standing firm, lasting.

evidence.note: “He is the living God, and enduring (וְקַיָּם) forever, and his kingdom shall not be destroyed.”
“Your kingdom shall be sure (קַיָּמָה) to you, after you know that the heavens rule.”

words.gloss: rise, arise, stand; rise from the dead; (aphel) raise up, establish
words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܩܡ (qām), its usual word for ἀνίστημι, ἐγείρω and ἵστημι (about 550 uses): Christ “is risen”, the dead will rise, God “raises up” a prophet, David and David’s seed, and every word “stands” on two or three witnesses.

stems.gloss: rise, arise; rise from the dead; stand

senses.definition: Of Christ, and of the dead at the last day: to rise to life.

evidence.note: “He is not here, for he is risen (ܩܡ), as he said.”
“The Lord is risen indeed.”
“He was buried, and rose (ܘܩܡ) on the third day according to the scriptures.”
“Now Christ is risen from the dead, the firstfruits of those who sleep.”
“Your brother will rise (ܩܐܡ)”; Martha: “I know that he will rise in the resurrection at the last day” (Jhn 11:24).
“The dead in Christ will rise (ܢܩܘܡܘܢ) first.”
“For this Christ died and rose (ܘܩܡ) and lived, that he might be Lord of the dead and the living.”
After ܩܘܡܝ (Mrk 5:41), “the girl arose (ܩܡܬ) and walked”.

senses.definition: To rise up to act; to arise on the scene; to stand and hold good.

evidence.note: “I will arise (ܐܩܘܡ) and go to my father.”
Deu 19:15: “at the mouth of two or three witnesses every word shall stand (ܬܩܘܡ).”
“Every house divided against itself shall not stand.”
“Another priest arises (ܩܐܡ) after the likeness of Melchizedek.”
Exo 1:8: “another king arose.”
“The men of Nineveh will rise up in the judgment with this generation.”

stems.gloss: raise up; raise from the dead; establish

senses.gloss: raise up (a person); raise from the dead
senses.definition: God’s raising up a prophet, a king, a seed, and his raising Jesus from the dead.

evidence.note: Deu 18:15: “A prophet will the Lord your God raise up (ܢܩܝܡ) for you from your brothers, like me.”
“He raised up (ܐܩܝܡ) for them David as king … of this man’s seed God has, according to promise, raised up (ܐܩܝܡ) for Israel Jesus the Saviour” (Act 13:22–23).
“That he raised (ܐܩܝܡܗ) him from the dead, no more to return to corruption.”
“He has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David.”
“Whom God raised up, having loosed the pains of death.”
“I will raise him up (ܐܩܝܡܝܘܗܝ) at the last day.”
Amo 9:11: “I will raise up (ܘܐܩܝܡ) the tabernacle of David that is fallen.”
“Raise up seed for his brother.”

senses.definition: To establish a law or a righteousness, to set up.

evidence.note: “Do we then make void the law through faith? God forbid: we establish (ܡܩܝܡܝܢܢ) the law.”
“He takes away the first, that he may establish (ܢܩܝܡ) the second.”
“Seeking to establish their own righteousness.”

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܩܝܡܬܐ (qyāmtā), “a rising”, its word for ἀνάστασις, resurrection (about 36 uses).

senses.definition: The rising of the dead to life, Christ’s first, and of the dead at the last day.

evidence.note: “Those who have done good to the resurrection (ܠܩܝܡܬܐ) of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment.”
“There will be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and the unjust.”
“Concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read …?”
“The Sadducees say there is no resurrection.”
David “spoke of the resurrection of the Christ, that his soul was not left in the grave.”
“Born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead.”
“This is the first resurrection.”
“They are sons of God, being sons of the resurrection.”

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܩܝܡܐ (qyāmā): a standing or rising, and what is made to stand between parties, a covenant or sworn pact (7 uses).

senses.definition: A binding agreement, something established.

evidence.note: To the Israelites belong “the adoption and the glory and the covenants (ܩܝܡܐ)”.
Over forty men made “this pact (ܩܝܡܐ)”, an oath to kill Paul.
Among the vices: men without a covenant (ܩܝܡܐ), for Greek ἀσυνθέτους, “covenant-breakers”.

senses.definition: A standing, the state of being in place; a rising.

evidence.note: “This child is set for the fall and the rising (ܩܝܡܐ) of many in Israel.”
“While the first tabernacle still had standing (ܩܝܡܐ).”
“We have no fixed standing-place”, for ἀστατοῦμεν.

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܩܝܡܐ (qayyāmā), for μένω and its kin: what remains and stands fast (13 uses), as Biblical Aramaic קַיָּם.

senses.definition: Standing fast, lasting.

evidence.note: Isa 40:8: “The word of our Lord abides (ܩܝܡܐ) forever.”
“Through the word of God, living and abiding.”
“Because he abides forever, his priesthood does not pass.”
“The firm foundation of God stands.”
“There remains a sabbath rest for the people of God.”

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܩܘܡܬܐ (qawmtā), for ἡλικία, “stature” (5 uses): the Aramaic form of קוֹמָה.

senses.definition: A person’s height; growth to full measure.

evidence.note: Zacchaeus “was small in stature (ܩܘܡܬܗ)”.
“Which of you by worrying can add one cubit to his stature?”
“Jesus grew in wisdom and in stature.”
“To the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ.”

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܩܘܡܐ, for ὀργυιά, a fathom: a measure of a man’s height standing, as Arabic qāmah is both stature and a measure (2 uses, one verse).

senses.definition: A measure of depth, a man’s height.

evidence.note: The sailors sounded and found twenty fathoms, then fifteen fathoms.

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܩܘܝܡܐ, once, for σωτηρία where food keeps men alive; Arabic qiwām is likewise the food that is a man’s support.

senses.definition: What keeps a person alive and on his feet.

evidence.note: Paul urges them to take food, “for this is for your sustenance (ܠܩܘܝܡܐ)”.

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܩܝܘܡܬܐ, once, for προστάτις: Phoebe as one who stood by and supported many. Its tie to the root is the verb’s “stand by”, which Geʿez qoma “stand by to protect” shares.

senses.definition: A woman who stands by others to help them.

evidence.note: Phoebe “has been a helper (ܩܝܘܡܬܐ) of many, and of me also”.

cognates.gloss: stand up, rise; stand still; rise against; come to pass (the Hour); (IV aqāma) set up, establish, observe, remain
cognates.note: The Hebrew senses side by side: rising from sitting, rising against an adversary, the Hour of resurrection “standing”, and in form IV setting a thing up and establishing a proof, as the hiphil does.

evidence.note: “He stood still … in his place … He, or it, stood up, or erect … And hence, He rose, i. e. from sitting or reclining … قَامَتِ السَّاعَةُ The resurrection, or the time thereof, came to pass … قَامَ عَلَيْهِ He rose up against him.”

“He set up, put up, set upright, a thing … He remained, continued, stayed … He observed, or duly performed, a religious, or moral, ordinance … أَقَامَ البَيِّنَةَ He established the evidence or proof.”

cognates.note: The same noun of place as מָקוֹם, and still with its first sense “where the feet stand”.

evidence.note: “The place of the feet; a standingplace … a place of continuance, stay, residence, or abode.”

cognates.gloss: stature, a man’s height standing; (qawām) stature; (qiwām) sustenance
cognates.note: As קוֹמָה, the height one stands to; qiwām, “the food that is a man’s support”, answers the Peshitta’s ܩܘܝܡܐ.

evidence.note: “The stature of a man; his height in a standing posture … tallness, height.”
“Stature, and goodly stature, or tallness, of a man … قِوَامٌ The food that is a man’s support; [his subsistence.]”

cognates.gloss: a people; a company or body of men
cognates.note: One reading of אַלְקוּם (Pro 30:31) takes it as the Arabic article with this word, “the band (of soldiers)”.

evidence.note: “A people, or body of persons composing a community … a company, or body … of men.”

cognates.note: In the Baal text KTU 1.10 II 17, 25, wyqm “and he rose”, and bʿpr qm aḫk “in the dust is your brother’s adversary”: the same participle use as Hebrew קָמִים, קָמַי.

evidence.locator: §93 Glossary, /q-w-m/ (p. 199 or 200; OCR only, page unverified); text §88.56 = KTU 1.10 II 17, 25
evidence.note: “/q-w-m/: yqm 1.10:II:17 = 88.56 ‘to rise’ (H. qām, yāqūm, Aram. qām, yəqūm, Arab. qāma, yaqūmu); part. qm 1.10:II:25 = 88.56 (‘one who is rising against’ >) ‘adversary’ (H. qām)”.

cognates.note: Recorded only in the root-set data; the Ugaritic passages were not read for this entry.

cognates.gloss: persist in; keep to (an agreement); (yiphil) raise, rouse
cognates.note: Punic “stick to the sales agreement” is the Hebrew “a vow stands”; the yiphil “raise, rouse (a god from sleep)” is the hiphil “raise up”.

evidence.note: “v. qal 1. PERSIST in doing something, KAI 9 A 2 … 2. STICK to an agreement, Trip. 51 … v. yiphʿil RAISE, ROUSE from sleep: See MQM ʾLM.”

cognates.gloss: place, spot; region; district; city; building; temple
cognates.note: The same noun as מָקוֹם, and like it used of a holy place: Punic “the [holy] place” (KAI 173.5).

evidence.note: “[Heb. maqom] n.m. 1. PLACE, SPOT, KAI 10.14/16 … 2. AREA, REGION … 3. DISTRICT of a city … 4. CITY … 5. STRUCTURE, BUILDING … 6. TEMPLE.”

cognates.note: Krahmalkov compares Hebrew קוֹמָה; “standing” in the community, but no Hebrew use of קוֹמָה has this sense, so it is not named on the word.

evidence.note: “[cf. Heb. qoma, ‘height’] n.f. RESPECT, HIGH REGARD, KAI 43.10 … KAI 165.4.”

cognates.gloss: stand; stand still; persist, endure; be ratified; rise against; stand by (to protect); (causative ኣቀመ) set up, establish, raise up (offspring)
cognates.note: Dillmann’s senses run with the Hebrew’s: “ratum esse” at Num 30:5, 8, 12 (vows stand), “resistere, insurgere” (rise against), and in the causative “erigere, statuere”, “stabilire”, and “suscitare … prolem” at Deu 25:7 and Rut 4:5, 10.

evidence.note: “stare, se sistere … e) perstare i. e. perdurare, constare … δ) ratum esse vel fieri Num. 30, 5. 8. 12; Matth. 18, 16 … g) resistere, insurgere … h) adesse alicui protegendo vel defendendo”; causative “a) erigere, statuere … c) stabilire … d) surgere vel prodire facere, excitare, suscitare … prolem, Deut. 25, 7. 8; Ruth 4, 5. 10.”

cognates.note: Dillmann cites it for the heights of Exo 25:10, 23 and Ezk 31:3, where the Hebrew has קוֹמָה.
A noun of place from the same root, as מָקוֹם.

evidence.note: “i) locus standi … statio; locus … Jos 10, 13 … 2 Par. 7, 6.”

cognates.gloss: stand up, rise; stand, exist; endure, hold good (Jewish Aramaic); קַיָּים existing, enduring, valid
cognates.note: The Targums and Talmud use it as scripture’s Aramaic does: “whose counsel will stand”, “stand up before a great man”; and קַיָּים of an oath that “holds good” and of a vow confirmed by the husband, against בָּטֵל “void”.

evidence.note: “(b. h.) to stand up, rise; to stand, exist”; II: “Targ. Gen. XXII, 3. Targ. Lev. XXV, 30 … Lev. R. s. 16 (ref. to Is. V, 19) נדע דמן הוא דקיימא … that we know whose counsel will stand.”
“(קוּם) existing, enduring, lasting; valid … so thy oath holds good for ever and ever; opp. בָּטֵל … thy vow is valid (confirmed by me).”

cognates.note: The Targums use it for Hebrew קוֹמָה and קוֹמְמִיּוּת (Targ. Y. Lev 26:13; Targ. Isa 10:33).

evidence.note: “= h. קוֹמָה. Targ. Y. Lev. XXVI, 13 … Targ. Is. X, 33.”

doctrine.statement: When the ark set out from Sinai, Moses said, “Arise, Yahweh, and let your enemies be scattered” (Num 10:35), and when it came to rest, “Return, Yahweh” (Num 10:36). Yahweh’s rising is his acting: “because of the oppression of the poor … now I will arise” (Psa 12:6); “Arise, O God, judge the earth, for you shall inherit all the nations” (Psa 82:8); he waits “for the day of my rising up to the prey”, to gather nations for judgment (Zep 3:8; Isa 2:19). The psalm that opens with Moses’ words (Psa 68:2) goes on to the ascent “on high, leading captivity captive” (Psa 68:19), which Paul applies to Christ’s ascension and his gifts to the ecclesia (Eph 4:8). From the verses: Yahweh rises from his place to save his people and judge their enemies, and the march of the ark, with Yahweh going before Israel to the land, pictures the work completed in Christ and to be completed when he judges the earth.

The dead lie down and do not rise “till the heavens are no more; they shall not awake, nor be roused out of their sleep” (Job 14:12). Rising is what God does for them: “your dead shall live, my corpses shall rise; awake and sing, dwellers in the dust” (Isa 26:19); “on the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live before him” (Hos 6:2). Not all are raised: of Judah’s oppressors, “they are dead, they shall not live; Raphaites, they shall not rise” (Isa 26:14; Psa 88:11). The Peshitta uses the same root throughout the New Testament: Christ “rose (ܘܩܡ) on the third day according to the scriptures” (1Co 15:4), “the dead in Christ will rise first” (1Th 4:16), “I will raise him up at the last day” (Jhn 6:40), and the resurrection is ܩܝܡܬܐ, “a rising”, of the just and the unjust, to life or to judgment (Jhn 5:29; Act 24:15). From the verses: death is a sleep in the dust, not a passing on to another life; the hope set before man is to be raised and stand up alive again, Christ first, then those who are his at his coming (1Co 15:20–23).

Yahweh promised Moses, “I will raise up for them a prophet from among their brothers, like you” (Deu 18:15, 18), and David, “I will raise up your seed after you, who shall come out of your body, and I will establish his kingdom” (2Sa 7:12); the prophets repeat it: a righteous Branch raised up to David (Jer 23:5), “David their king, whom I will raise up for them” (Jer 30:9), the fallen tent of David raised up (Amo 9:11). Peter applies Deu 18:15 to Jesus (Act 3:22–26), James applies Amo 9:11 to the calling of the Gentiles (Act 15:14–17), and Paul says that God “raised up David to be their king … of this man’s seed God has, according to promise, raised up for Israel a Saviour, Jesus”, and then that he “raised him from the dead” (Act 13:22–23, 30–34), the Peshitta using ܐܩܝܡ for both. From the verses: the promised one is “raised up” from among his brothers and from David’s body, a man of Israel, and God’s raising him from the dead is the fulfilment of the same promise.

What Yahweh says, he makes stand: “Has he spoken, and will he not make it stand?” (Num 23:19). He “establishes” his covenant with Noah and with Abraham’s seed (Gen 9:11; 17:7), the oath sworn to the fathers (Gen 26:3; Deu 9:5), and his good word to Israel (Jer 33:14); “the counsel of Yahweh, it shall stand” (Pro 19:21; Isa 46:10), while the plots of kings “shall not stand” (Isa 7:7). “The word of our God shall stand forever” (Isa 40:8), and Peter says of it, “this is the word which was preached to you” (1Pe 1:25). Paul, teaching faith, says “we establish the law” (Rom 3:31), and the Peshitta calls the covenants of Israel ܩܝܡܐ, “what is made to stand” (Rom 9:4). From the verses: the promises to Abraham and David are not set aside; God makes them stand, and the gospel preached is that same enduring word.

Israel set out from Sinai “for the place of which Yahweh said, I will give it to you” (Num 10:29), and in the land the feasts and sacrifices were bound to “the place which Yahweh your God shall choose to put his name there” (Deu 12:5; 16:2, 6). Jeremiah warned that a chosen place could be given up: “go to my place which was in Shiloh … and see what I did to it”, and so would he do to the house called by his name (Jer 7:12–14). Jesus told the woman at the well that the hour was coming when men would worship the Father neither in Samaria nor in Jerusalem, but in spirit and truth (Jhn 4:20–24); the rulers feared the Romans would “take away our place and nation” (Jhn 11:48); Stephen was accused of saying Jesus would “destroy this place” (Act 6:13–14), and answered from Isa 66:1, “what is the place of my rest?” (Act 7:48–49). From the verses: the place was given for a time, as Shiloh had been, and its overthrow, foretold by Jesus (Luk 21:5–6, 20), came on that generation when Jerusalem and its temple were destroyed in AD 70.

Before the flood Yahweh said, “every יְקוּם that I have made I will blot out from the face of the ground” (Gen 7:4), and it was done: “he blotted out every יְקוּם that was on the face of the ground, from man to beast … and only Noah was left, and those with him in the ark” (Gen 7:23). Jesus says “the flood came and destroyed them all” (Luk 17:27; Mat 24:39), and Peter that “the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished” (2Pe 3:6). From the verses: everything that stood and lived on the land perished except what was in the ark; the flood covered the whole earth, not one region of it.

note: Drafted 2026-11-13 for Numbers 10 (קוּמָה, Num 10:35; מָקוֹם, Num 10:29; also הֵקִימוּ, Num 10:21), with Lev 23:15–16 tied in through קָמָה at Deu 16:9. Root key קומ is the database’s (root table: Hollow, 623 occurrences). DATABASE FAULT: word_info.root for most Hebrew tokens of the verb (וַיָּקָם, קוּם, יָקוּם, הֵקִים, קוּמָה at Num 10:35 …) is לבב, not קומ, so lexicon-brief files them as “analysed as a verb of another root” and leaves them out; the stem counts here (qal 459, hiphil 146, piel 11, polel 4, hithpolel 4, hophal 3) were taken from surface_entry key s.av.aa joined to morph_cell. lexicon-support may undercount the verb. Key s.av.aa also counts 5 Aramaic peal tokens and 6 קָמָה tokens; xs.ad.aa (Aramaic verb) also counts about 37 Hebrew qal tokens by spelling. s.av.al (Psa 139:21 וּבִתְקוֹמְמֶיךָ, one token) is added to the verb’s keys as a hithpolel. Left out: zero-token cross-reference keys j.da.ad, m.df.an, m.df.av, s.aa.ac, s.av.ah, s.bj.ac, s.bu.ae, s.bu.ag, w.bn.ag, w.bn.ah, xs.af.ad, a.du.ab. Left out as not of this root: קוֹף “ape” (s.av.as, 1Ki 10:22; 2Ch 9:21), a loan, cf. Egyptian gjf “vervet” (TLA tla166670). Names not entered (none occurs in Lev 23 or Num 10): persons יְקַמְיָה Jekamiah (s.av.an), יָקִים Jakim (s.av.aj), יְקַמְעָם Jekameam (s.av.ao); places יָקְמְעָם Jokmeam (s.av.ap), קָמוֹן Kamon (s.av.af); the people קוֹעַ Koa (s.av.ar, Ezk 23:23), whose tie to the root is not clear. Akkadian has no cognate (Oracc candidates qamû “burn”, qemû “grind” are other roots; Akkadian uses izuzzu for “stand”). Syriac: SEDRA root 1632 (ܩܡ), lexemes 2765 ܩܘܝܡܐ, 2766 ܩܡ, 2767 ܩܘܡܐ, 2768 ܩܘܡܬܐ, 2769 ܩܝܘܡܐ, 2770 ܩܝܡܐ (adj.), 2771 ܩܝܡܐ (noun), 2772 ܩܝܡܬܐ; the brief reported no Peshitta root, so these were found by hand; Payne Smith not consulted. Lemma pointing of the Syriac words is approximate.
